articleTitle: The knowledge based approach for emitter identification
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Current Electronic Warfare (EW) systems use algorithmic processing methods which are inflexible and do not fully utilise available sources of a priori information. The EW systems of the future are required to react faster and with greater accuracy to an extremely complex electromagnetic environment. This paper presents the role of knowledge based processing methods and how they may be applied to emitters (radars) identification.

articleTitle: Accuracy of the passive tracking systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper, the problems of increasing the accuracy and resistance of a passive tracking systems (PTS) which operates in conditions of interference are solved. We suppose that the PTS are multipurpose wide-band synchronous automated data communication systems (ADCS). The real accuracy of filtering X and Y coordinates of the flying objects by the of PTS was verified through simulation. The results of simulation may by used in the practical application of PTS.

articleTitle: Analysis of radar echo from a helicopter rotor hub
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The problem of rotor hub echo usage for hovering helicopter detection and classification with a radar system is presented. A theoretical model of rotor hub backscatter is compared with results obtained from radar signal analysis. The possibility of identifying a helicopter by the characteristic "shelf" in its Doppler echo spectrum is explained, along with analysis of conditions necessary for detecting this characteristic.

articleTitle: On application of a pulse method in detecting living objects
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Demonstrates the pulse method's possibilities in living object detection by a system, based on a 30 GHz sampling oscilloscope. It is shown that biological objects can be observed even in still and breathless condition due to involuntary movements and palpation of the heart.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental investigations of a bilevel 'Lange' coupler
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: An interdigitated coupler in which two pairs of strips are placed on both sides of a thin dielectric layer, connected to a main substrate, is theoretically and experimentally investigated. Frequency-dependent parameters of a 3 dB coupler are calculated as a function of thickness of the thin dielectric. An optimum thickness giving a very good matching and high directivity of the coupler, is revealed. Parasitic resonances, appearing in vicinity of 2/spl times/ centre frequency of the coupler, strongly deteriorating coupler performance, are efficiently suppressed using an additional planar bonding. Measured coupler characteristics are also given.

articleTitle: A simple method for permittivity measurement using microwave resonant cavity
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new simple method for permittivity measuring of the lossless dielectric material using microwave resonant cavity, is presented in this paper. Also, the proposed method can be applied to the real part of the complex permittivity measurement of low loss dielectric material.

articleTitle: Surface acoustic wave devices: a rewarding past, a significant present, and a promising future
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The concept of a thin-film metal interleaved comb structure (interdigital transducer) on a polished piezoelectric plate, was first introduced in 1965 as an efficient means for the generation and detection of surface acoustic waves. There followed a wealth of ideas and a flurry of developments which produced frequency and time domain devices significantly enhancing the signal processing capabilities of microwave systems. These devices, many of which were first implemented in military radar and communication systems, covered a frequency range from 10 MHz to well over 1.0 GHz. Today, the diversity of SAW device applications in electronic products, the number of manufacturers, the total number of devices manufactured, and the employees worldwide involved in the design, development, and manufacture of SAW devices, speaks of a very robust technology with a promising future. This paper reviews the basic piezoelectric substrate based device concepts, characterize present activities, and take a look at where SAW technology is headed in the near future.

articleTitle: Digital microwave phase shifters with integrated switches
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper presents digital microwave phase shifters with integrated switches. The design formulas and experimental results of practical circuits operating in L-band are described. These circuits can be used in many different communication systems.

articleTitle: An effective coordinates conversion algorithm for radar-controlled anti-aircraft systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The authors present methods of converting target coordinates useful for geographic specifics of the area of Poland and which may be used in home radar systems. Here they consider algorithms converting spherical coordinates of the airborne object detected by the radar of the air defence system to geodetic coordinates used in the system as a whole.

articleTitle: On "/spl alpha/-features" of electrical waves above impedance plane
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper, using the concept and tools of fractional calculus, the author introduces a definition for "/spl alpha/-features" of electrical waves, which spreads above an impedance plane. Illustrative examples of calculation of dependency z-components of the wave from the frequency and decelerating parameters are presented. Salient features of E/sub z/ are discussed. Some physical insights for such "/spl alpha/-features" are also given.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave phase shifters based on ferrite dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Dielectric waveguides made of ferrites of rectangular cross section are experimentally studied at frequencies 30-120 GHz. These waveguides were used for development of electrically controlled phase shifters with longitudinal magnetic field. The advantages of the reported waveguides and phase shifters are as follows: broad band, simple construction, low loss and price cost.

articleTitle: Planar resonator sensor for moisture measurements
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the paper a model of microwave planar resonator sensor has been presented. The structure of resonator sensor is described. A dielectric material is placed above microstrip ring resonator. As a consequence, the parameters of resonator: resonance frequency, quality factor, and resonance transmission change in relation to the permittivity of the material. The first results of measurements are presented. The sensor may be used for nondestructive measurements of the moisture content of dielectric materials like grain or sand.

articleTitle: Investigation of the HTS microstrip filters based on dual-mode ring resonators
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The design and realization of the HTS dual-mode microstrip ring resonator narrow-band filters is presented. As a design tool LIBRA has been used. Two types of superconductors and substrates have been used: YBCO on sapphire and TBCCO on LaAlO/sub 3/. Two-pole Tchebyshev type filters and four-pole elliptic filters have been realized.

articleTitle: Automated noise figure measurement using computer and spectrum analyzer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: After a short review, several measurement techniques are considered. The "Y factor" method is described in detail. After a mathematical description, for the given measurement setup using a spectrum analyzer, has been derived, a computer program for the automatic calibration and measurement was written. The measurement results are compared with those obtained by using noise figure meter HP 8970B, and has been found to be in very good agreement.

articleTitle: High power variable attenuator with PIN diodes
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A concept and design of a high power attenuator for the X-band have been presented. The attenuation is controlled by two PIN diodes. A circuit is based on a ring coupler and it is configured as a reflective one with two external matched loads. Due to poor switching properties of the diodes in the X-band, a special transforming circuit has been proposed. Any attenuation between 1.5 and 20 dB can be obtained with the input VSWR not exceeding 1.5 over the band from 9 to 9.8 GHz.

articleTitle: The effect of parasitic inductances in distributed amplifiers
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The gain-bandwidth relations of distributed amplifiers (DA) are analyzed If is shown that the amplifier performance is uniquely related to the properties of the active elements and the electrical length of the transmission lines between them. It is proved that the parasitic inductance of the connections between the embedding network and the transistors strongly distorts the gain characteristics. The paper proposes the so-called V-shape connection structure which overcomes the above mentioned disadvantages.

articleTitle: New closed solutions of the linear antenna synthesis problem according to amplitude radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the linear antenna case, the synthesis problem according to prescribed amplitude pattern is solved analytically with a limited numbers of complex parameters to be calculated. These parameters are defined from the set of transcendental equations. As they are nonunique, the optimal solution is chosen from the all obtained solutions. A measure of the synthesis effectivity is offered. The case, when the given amplitude pattern is constant inside the limited angle, is considered in detail and numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: A planar microwave frequency discriminator
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The topology of proposed microwave frequency discriminator circuit involves the elements of one type in the form of quadrature couplers. The structure does not include either transmission line crossings or phase shifters, typically required under such circumstances. The complete frequency discriminator can be made as one planar IC. Such a structure of the frequency discriminator was made and investigated in the L and S frequency band.

articleTitle: Investigation of InGaAs p-i-n photodiode for optical-microwave mixing process
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: An InGaAs p-i-n photodiode, operating at 1.3 /spl mu/m has been fabricated and used in an optical-microwave mixer configuration. The DC characteristics, diode capacitance for various incident optical power as well as frequency dependence of responsivity and reflection coefficient up to 3 GHz were investigated. Bias and local oscillator power level dependence of optical-microwave mixing process is reported and discussed.

articleTitle: Application of the multigrid method in determination of SAR distribution in hyperthermia treatment of gyneacological cancers
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper the method for the 3D computer simulation of SAR distribution during hyperthermia treatment of cervical cancers is presented. A gynealogical applicator for brachytherapy treatment acts as a hyperthermia intracavitar applicator. The numerical analysis is carried out by means of a technique incorporating adaptive grid refinement and multilevel relaxations.

articleTitle: Four bit phase shifter for the L band
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A four bit phase shifter for a phased array has been described. The phase shifter has been realised in a hybrid MIC technique with PIN diodes used as switching elements. The circuit consists of three bits realised as a periodically loaded line and one based on a hybrid 3 dB coupler. The three first bits have special tuning elements for the fine tuning of the required phase shift. The phase shift error was not greater than 3 degrees. Average loss was about 1.5 dB, while maximum amplitude unbalance was 0.3 dB.

articleTitle: Direct analog synthesis modules for an X-band frequency source
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Some design considerations of frequency synthesis modules are presented. The module consists of a bank of crystal or SAW resonator stabilized oscillators and frequency multipliers, connected to the output via a multithrow switch. Phase noise performance of SAW oscillators vs. crystal oscillators is compared. It is shown that better spurious signals rejection can be obtained when frequency multipliers are placed before the switch, despite the worse isolation of the switch at higher frequencies. In this configuration, keying the multipliers allows for further isolation improvement.

articleTitle: C-band high power PIN diode switch
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A C-band PIN diode switch for a high power T/R module is presented in the paper. The electrical and mechanical design of the PIN diode switch with compensation of the parasitic series inductance of the diodes is described. This compensation allows us to achieve an isolation of more than 40 dB with use of only one pair of PIN diodes.

articleTitle: High frequency interconnections using electrically conductive adhesives
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Results from measurements and simulation of high frequency interconnections are used to obtain an electrical model of the adhesive joint based on the physical parameters involved. Isotropically conductive adhesive joints can be used at microwave frequencies at least up to 30 GHz. Results indicate that the electrical performance of these connections is comparable to that of solder joints.

articleTitle: Performance characteristics of pulse radar detection using neural networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the problem of sidelobe suppression in a matched filter for wideband signals with using the neural network (NN) approach. Principle performance characteristics of a NN detection procedure such as NN structure and parameters, its impulse response and amplitude characteristics, output signal probability density function and detection probabilities have been investigated. The simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: High unloaded Q waveguide-dielectric resonators modes
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Waveguide-dielectric resonators (WDR) with partial E-plane filling of the waveguide are considered. The eigen LM/sub mnk/ modes problem of such a WDR has been solved by the mode matching method. Theoretically and experimentally, the spectrum eigen modes dynamics dependency on the dielectric insets geometry was investigated. The calculated results are in good agreement with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Radio-node upconversion in millimeter-wave fiber-radio distribution systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Optical generation and distribution of millimeter waves have become an intensive research topic recently. A main field of possible applications is the millimeter-wave (MMW) wireless distribution of broadband data in future fiber-radio cellular systems. In this paper a new approach for the generation of MMW carriers in a fiber-radio system is presented. Utilizing radio-node upconversion of the distributed information signals and subcarrier multiplex (SCM) technique, problems of chromatic dispersion and radiofrequency interference are avoided.

articleTitle: "MICROEXPERT"-the computer expert system for microwave oscillators design: an initial approach
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: An expert system, called MICROEXPERT, for designing microwave oscillators with multiple active devices and power combiners with a TM/sub 010/ mode cavity is presented. A logical structure of the system composed of deciding rules which should be followed during the design process of the oscillators is shown. The system is based on real engineering data and has a packet of files which consists of oscillator optimization programs, databases, knowledge base subprograms and supervising (main) program.

articleTitle: Application of artificial intelligence in radar resource management
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Multifunction radar resource management problems are considered in this paper. A classical solution is shown and compared to a system proposed here in which artificial intelligence methods are used. Neural networks and expert systems are the main tools of the artificial intelligence. An application of the expert system in a signal structure and parameters selection unit is presented and its features are described. Test results are satisfactory and are discussed.

articleTitle: Impedance bandwidth characteristics of normal and inverted stacked microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Stacked microstrip antenna has been reported to provide broader bandwidth by stagger tuning dual (or multiple) resonators. A theoretical study of normal and inverted diagonally fed square patch configurations is carried out to examine their impedance bandwidth characteristics. It is concluded in this paper that apart from providing the radome effect, the inverted patch is superior in performance.

articleTitle: FODEL(R) photoimageable technology in microwave applications
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: New circuit technologies capable of delivering high volume production, low cost microwave hybrids are still being sought. Advanced thick film technology offers new solutions suitable for microwave performance: the etching of fired thick films and the photoimaging of photosensitive thick films. Both techniques, using novel thick film materials and photopatterning gives a performance comparable with thin film techniques at significantly lower cost.

articleTitle: Design of NRD-guide bandpass filters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper presents a method of the synthesis of an NRD-guide bandpass filter based on a half-wave step-impedance prototype filter. The only wave parameter required to design a filter is the reflection coefficient S(11/sub i/). A 3-pole NRD-guide filter with Chebyshev 0.1 dB equiripple characteristic was designed. The center frequency was chosen to be f/sub 0/-9.5 GHz and pass band to 1.9%. The filter was verified numerically using 3D FDTD simulator Quick-wave.

articleTitle: Design of E-tee diplexers having closely spaced frequency channels in the upper part of a waveguide operating range
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Some configurations of E-tee diplexers are synthesized and analyzed for the case of closely spaced channel frequency bands in the upper part of a rectangular waveguide operating range. The results of rigorous electromagnetic synthesis and analysis of the millimeter-wave diplexers with all-metal E-plane insert channel filters are presented.

articleTitle: Wide-band microstrip and coplanar-type 3 dB directional couplers with quasi-ideal sections of coupled lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Wide-band 3 dB couplers with two different microstrip quasi-symmetric tightly coupled-line sections have been designed, fabricated and measured. The calculated frequency-dependent characteristics of these couplers are compared with measured responses. It is shown that a multi-section coupler with asymmetric coupled lines as the centre section can compose an optimum 90/spl deg/ coupler, if correcting lengths of transmission line are added. A coplanar-type MMIC version of this wide-band 3 dB coupler is proposed.

articleTitle: Microwave diplexer with direct coupled filters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The characteristics and advantages of direct coupled filers are considered in this paper. After removing the two resonators from the filter structure, the characteristics of such a filter are similar to single terminated filter. These filters can be connected in series. Using 90/spl deg/ phase shifters is equivalent to the connection in series of two two-ports. Experimental results of a diplexer covering the frequency band (0.5-1.5) GHz are presented.

articleTitle: High dynamic range octave-band microwave frequency measurement systems up to 18 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The results of developmental work on wide-band systems for microwave frequency measurement are presented in this paper. Based on the interferometric frequency measurement method the systems for octave-band frequency measurement from 1 GHz to 8 GHz have been examined. Thanks to applying limiting amplifiers the systems are characterized by a very high dynamic range either for CW or a very short pulses. All these systems can operate in the -40/spl deg/C-65/spl deg/C temperature range.

articleTitle: Synthesis of nonuniformly spaced arrays using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The application of a genetic algorithm to the design of nonuniformly spaced, linear arrays is presented. Looking for positioning of elements in large arrays for low sidelobe levels involves examining a huge number of possibilities, in order to find the best solution. A genetic algorithm, unlike many conventional optimization methods, can optimize such problems. In this paper the genetic algorithm is applied to find the element positions in the 48-element linear array with uniform excitation that produces minimum sidelobe level The comparison of the effectiveness of the proposed approach and the several traditional optimization algorithms is also presented.

articleTitle: Multiple oscillator frequency synthesizer with common phase lock loop
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The use of several narrowband VCOs with a common phase lock loop in a multichannel frequency source provides certain advantages over more conventional concepts based on a single broadband VCO and microwave switches. Multiple oscillator design offers better phase noise performance and less complicated microwave circuitry. These advantages are particularly distinct in case of a synthesizer with multiple outputs assigned for separate, narrowband frequency channels.

articleTitle: Range and azimuth estimation using raw data in DSP-based radar system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the paper a problem of estimation of target position in a modern DSP-based radar system is considered. The processes of target detection and estimation are separated. Raw radar data supplied to the detection block are buffered in large RAM memory and then partially post-processed by the estimation block in areas nearby detected targets. Such an approach allows for more elaborate estimation algorithms than using joint detection and estimation. We have adopted curve-fitting procedures for both azimuth and range estimation. Simulation results prove good performance even for small signal to noise ratios.

articleTitle: On operation of self-phased arrays under conditions of multipath propagation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper gives an analysis of operation of a self-phased array under conditions of multipath propagation (either reflections or jamming signals). A general method for the calculation of directivity of such an array has been proposed. Influence of reflections by way of the pilot signal channel as well as by way of the primary signal channel is taken into account. Some limitations of the approach proposed before have been pointed out and overcome in this paper. It has been shown that an essential reduction in directivity is possible in the case of weak pilot signal or large (close to unity) reflection coefficient.

articleTitle: Adaptive aperture formation matched with radiometry image spatial spectrum
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new approach to radiometry image formation based on the matching of image characteristics with aperture synthesis is proposed. A quantitative analysis and comparison with the conventional method of radiometry imaging are performed.

articleTitle: Cylindrical antenna array feeding network for electronic scanning
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper presents a cylindrical antenna array feeding network with electronically scanning beam. On the basis of the presented numerical results, the antenna was designed and constructed. The measured parameters of the feeding network of the cylindrical antenna array are presented. An agreement between the experimental results and the design is obtained.

articleTitle: Analysis of the dynamical chaos in a cavity with an array of active devices
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Excitation of electromagnetic dynamical chaos in a cavity with an array of active devices is simulated. Poincare sections, power spectra, and sensitive dependence of solutions on initial conditions are analyzed. The chaos is shown to appear when the nonlinear field-array coupling constant G>1.

articleTitle: Novel dispersive delay line: technology and results
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: SAW dispersive delay line with a novel IDT of variable finger widths and spacings has been manufactured and measured. It was found that it achieve very close agreement with the required parameters.

articleTitle: Comparison of planar antenna feed networks with Wilkinson and coupled-line power dividers
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Parallel and series planar antenna array feed networks composed of Wilkinson-type and coupled-line power dividers are examined. Phase characteristics are compared in a wide band. Some optimal behaviour of a parallel coupled-line power divider is observed. The measured characteristics of selected coupled-line power dividers are also presented.

articleTitle: Tunable UHF TV channel power filter optimization
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper the design and realization of a mechanically tunable TEM-mode channel power filter for the UHF TV band are presented. A three-stage coaxial resonator filter was made without tunable capacitors and with minimum necessary adjustment by two inductive couplings. Calculated and experimental results agreed very well.

articleTitle: Loop directional coupler for rectangular waveguides with small dimensions
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper includes the following topics: an approximate expression for coupling; conditions for flat coupling in the full operating waveguide band; theoretical and experimental results of coupling; and the directivity and VSWR of the main and auxiliary lines.

articleTitle: Analysis of the nonreciprocal ferrite phase shifter with nonuniform cross-section
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A section of nonreciprocal ferrite phase shifter based on the waveguide with nonuniform cross-section was analyzed by means of the perturbation method. Basic fields are calculated with finite difference frequency domain method for the structure filled with dielectric toroid. The toroid's nonuniform magnetic permeability was accurately approximated by locally uniform sections. Calculated nonreciprocal phase shifts correspond to the measured ones.

articleTitle: Efficient matched filtering of signal with polyphase Frank coded sequences
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The efficient implementation of the matched filter for the signal with polyphase frank coded sequences is presented. To minimize the complexity of the matched filter hardware and software implementation, the moving discrete Fourier transform (MDFT) algorithm is used. The solution proposed here permits the optional number of the signal samples per code element.

articleTitle: Progress in time-domain electromagnetic modelling
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This contribution provides a short review of new developments in time-domain modelling. Improvements in the basic simulation algorithm as well as in preprocessing and postprocessing environment are addressed. Their combination results in user-friendly software tools competitive to the more classical frequency-domain simulators. As an example, QuickWave-3D software package is presented. Since the annual number of scientific papers on the time-domain modelling experiences an almost exponential growth, the list of publications given herein is inevitably selective. An interested reader will find more references in our previous reports [1991-96] and may also consult an FDTD database [1997].

articleTitle: Two bistatic target signatures: the bistatic equations and the bistatic polarisation fork
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The object of this article is to present two mathematical supports which allow a better knowledge of the target in a bistatic polarimetric radar configuration. These aids are firstly the nine bistatic target equations which link together the new sixteen bistatic target parameters, and secondly the bistatic polarisation fork which visualises the sixteen characteristic polarisation states of the target on the Poincare sphere.

articleTitle: Scalar permeability measurements of microwave ferrites using lumped circuit, coaxial line, and resonance techniques
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Complex scalar permeability measurement results of microwave ferrites at frequencies from 1 Hz to 20 GHz are presented. Three different techniques were used to perform the measurements. The method chosen depended on frequency and magnetic loss. At low frequencies, 1-10/sup 5/ Hz, we applied lumped parameter circuit techniques. With this technique nonlinear permeability effects were measured. At higher frequencies, from 1 MHz up to gyromagnetic resonance, coaxial transmission line techniques were used. At frequencies above gyromagnetic resonance, a dielectric ring resonator technique was used. By combining all three methods, the real and imaginary parts of sample permeability, with magnetic loss factors that vary from 10/sup -5/ to 10/sup 2/, may be measured. In addition, nonlinear effects in ferrite materials and saturation magnetization may be evaluated.

articleTitle: Microstrip patch antenna for a GSM 1800 base station
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A small array of microstrip patches is presented. It has been designed, fabricated and tested to be used in a GSM 1800 base station antenna. A partial compensation of the free space attenuation along a sector cell is provided.

articleTitle: Outlines of signal detection by passive multisite radar systems (MSRSs)
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Principal results of the detection theory for passive MSRSs obtained on the basis of a unified approach in the frequency domain are outlined. Optimum and suboptimum detection algorithms for signals with deterministic and quasideterministic correlation matrices in a background of noise and external interferences are presented and analyzed.

articleTitle: Designing of filters by using Kuroda's identities
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper six new and two known Kuroda's identities for the transformation of filters with real transmission zeros are presented. The transformed filters are convenient for physical realization of microwave filters and diplexers in printed circuit technology. The correctness of procedure is verified by transforming one filter of the third degree.

articleTitle: Derivation of the Plessky solution to my dispersive equation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Acoustic surface transversal modes, closely similar to Bleustein-Gulyaev waves, propagating under heavy periodic metal strips on a piezoelectric substrate are considered. STW, like BG wave, has wave number close to the cut-off wave number of the bulk wave that constitutes it. The theory of ST wave propagation gives more complicated dispersive equation than the one known for Rayleigh wave. Here we show explicit solutions to the dispersive equation resulting from the spectral theory, and compare it with the known Plessky formula.

articleTitle: Short wave EHF high-sensitivity two-frequency converter
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A two-frequency converter of the 1.5 mm band is developed and investigated. The design peculiarities of the two-frequency converters on a quasi-optical transmission line metallo-dielectric waveguide are discussed. Such a converter of frequency is tested in a radiometric receiver for measurement of the ozone content in the atmosphere.

articleTitle: Acoustic pseudo-surface modes-a complete characterization
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: High velocity pseudo surface acoustic waves (HVPSAWs) are currently widely investigated in SAW literature as promising for high frequency SAW devices. A complete characterization of such complex modes is proposed that can be used in the theory of the key structures of microwave acoustics: IDTs, MSCs, and groove grating reflectors of HVPSAW. Numerical examples are presented.

articleTitle: A broadband rotary joint for L-band
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The design of a flat rotary joint with a very broad operating frequency band is described. The solution proposed here enables practical elimination of signal amplitude/phase and impedance changes considered as a function of rotation angle. Low transmission and reflection loss have also been achieved. According to experimental results presented in this paper, fractional bandwidth of the model exceeds 50%, with maximum SWR of 1.8.

articleTitle: The design of the low noise GaAs MMICs broadband amplifiers
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper presents an approach to the problem of low-noise broadband MMIC amplifiers in the low GHz frequency ranges implemented at the Institute of Electronics Fundamentals. The performance of the well know resistive feedback amplifier is compared to the novel structure with capacitive lossless feedback. The new circuit has one of the best noise properties ever reported in the decade bandwidth.

articleTitle: Education oriented automated system for antenna radiation pattern measurement
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The setup for the radiation pattern measurement constructed at Technical University of Gdansk (TUG) is described. It consists of a MM-wave anechoic chamber and uses scalar network analyzer as a microwave receiver. The system is controlled by special HP-Vee program via GPIB interface. The results of experimental verification of properties of the system (repeatability, accuracy of side lobe level (SLL) measurement) showed that it can be successfully used for educational purposes as well as for some professional ones.

articleTitle: Linking of the elementary detections with using the neural network model in radar with two dimensional electronic scanning
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the paper the neural network model assigned to elementary detections linking the neighbour elevation antenna beam positions is described. The detections originate from the same target. They are given in a 3D search radar with two dimensional electronic scanning. The results of tests realized under conditions of one or two targets present show that the neural network model is useful for elementary detections linking and its further development is of interest.

articleTitle: Characterization of circular waveguide containing chiral rod
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Here we study the electromagnetic properties of circular waveguides containing a lossy isotropic chiral rod. The effects of the chirality on the polarisation state (electromagnetic field rotation and axial ratio AR) of the fundamental mode propagating in the guide are discussed and verified experimentally.

articleTitle: X-band pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance spectrometer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: X-Band pulsed EPR spectrometer designed and constructed in Wroclaw UT is described. The spectrometer has been designed as a modular system which makes it easy to upgrade. In the microwave path a power pulse amplifier with traveling wave tube (P/sub out/=350 W) is used. Pulse EPR signals are recorded with a fast digital storage oscilloscope of LeCroy (9361, 2.5 GS/s), supported with hardware mathematical option (WP02) performing FFT calculations. The system is fully controlled with PC computer via a GPIB interface.

articleTitle: Analysis of shielded anisotropic dielectric resonators using FDFD and the Arnoldi method
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Finite difference frequency domain (FDFD) formulation, based on Yee's mesh, is used for determination of resonant frequencies of rotationally symmetric shielded anisotropic dielectric resonators. Azimuthal field components are eliminated using divergence equation thereby reducing the size of eigenproblem and avoiding spurious eigenvalues. A resulting eigenproblem is solved by means of the Arnoldi method. Calculations are very efficient and accurate.

articleTitle: A broadband technique for one-port calibration of VNA
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A broadband versatile technique for precision one-port calibration of a vector network analyzer (VNA) is presented. It is an extension of a previous sliding short method accommodating, however, a broader class of calibration devices, such as delayed short and open circuits. It features a high measurement redundancy that allows the delays and losses of these devices to be determined during the calibration. The new method is suitable for characterization of low-loss two-ports.

articleTitle: Statistical estimation of antenna's selectivity
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper discusses an approach to antenna's selectivity estimation from point of view of the statistical theory of EMC. This approach is based on statistical model of the EM environment. Different statistical criteria to estimation of filter's selectivity are proposed, The use of this criteria enable us to determine functional dependences of selectivity of spatial filters on EM environment parameters. In order to solve this problem, a powerful algorithm based on Monte-Carlo simulation was used.

articleTitle: Single-toroid nonreciprocal latching ferrite phase shifter in modified waveguide
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper presents the concept of a modified waveguide cross section of a single-toroid nonreciprocal latching ferrite phase shifter as a method for cut-off of the first higher-order LSE and LSM modes for improving electrical performance.

articleTitle: Dispersive filter having nonperiodical IDT with apodization
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper is devoted mainly to the analysis of a dispersive filter having an unapodized periodical IDT and a nonperiodical IDT with apodization. The problem to be discussed is the reduction of the Fresnel ripples in the spectrum of nonperiodical structure. The dispersive transducer is apodized by a function such as the reverse form of the amplitude response of a signal with linear frequency modulation. The results of calculations as well as the outcome of experimental investigations for the chosen B=20 MHz, T=10 /spl mu/s, f/sub 0/=70 MHz values are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Coplanar microwave sensor for industrial measurements
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A concept of using distributed microwave coplanar sensors for nondestructive industrial measurements is explored. Basic properties of electromagnetic wave propagation in transmission lines loaded with test objects are discussed. An example of a coplanar sensor and the principles of its use in industry is outlined.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic waves scattering by dielectric and conducting cylinders in rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Scattering by a circular dielectric or perfectly conducting cylinder of any radius and any height in a rectangular waveguide oriented perpendicularly to the wide wall is considered. The electromagnetic field is represented by cylindrical eigenfunctions of the waveguide and dielectric medium, and the boundary conditions problem is solved strictly. Computed reflection and transmission coefficients are compared with the experimental results. The algorithm can be used for measurement purposes and the development of microwave devices.

articleTitle: Characteristic impedance of a cylindrical-rectangular coaxial line with offset inner circular conductor
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper, characteristic impedance of a Cylindrical-Rectangular (C-R) coaxial line is found for a line with a circular inner conductor of any arbitrary position inside an outer rectangular conductor. Results are given in the form of families of curves of characteristic impedance of the line vs. the diameter of the inner conductor and its orientation inside the rectangle. For symmetrical cases they are very close to the exact solutions.

articleTitle: On frequency stability of transmitter in LFMCW MTD radar
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the paper the requirements for the frequency stability of a transmitter in LFMCW MTD radar are considered. The linear model of carrier frequency rate is assumed. Relationships for range and velocity resolutions are derived. For explanatory reasons calculations for definite parameters of the sounding signals are performed. The considerations carried out lead to the conclusion that the requirements for frequency stability in relation to the velocity resolution are not stronger than for the range resolution.

articleTitle: A high power amplifiers for L-band transmitter with AM modulation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The 12 W class-A amplifier and the 500 W class-C pulsed amplifier for a transmitter with AM modulation are described. The designed linear amplifier, with GaAs MESFETs, exhibits a nonlinear distortion coefficient better than 20% for 60% AM modulation. The multistage class-C amplifier, based on bipolar transistors for IFF systems, assures 12% bandwidth and short pulse rise time T/sub r//spl les/100 ns.

articleTitle: A new method of the design and technology of PIN diodes
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Thermal and series resistance of semiconductor devices, especially high power devices such as high power PIN diodes, is a matter of major importance. This paper presents a new principle of the design and technology of high power PIN diodes which enables a significant reduction in the parasitic thermal and series resistance of the diodes.

articleTitle: A set-up to determine energy absorption during microwave heating
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A set-up to measure energy absorption by the material placed in a microwave oven (resonator) operating with high level of power is described. The base of the developed procedure is a determination of the incident power and relation of the reflected to incident signal in the waveguiding high power structure. Measurement accuracy of the system is estimated.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of MM-wave TEDs using an improved energy and momentum balance electron transport model
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: An efficient method for the numerical simulation of MM-wave transferred electron devices in a frequency range around 40 GHz has been presented. The improved energy and momentum balance model (EMB) of electron transport has been applied to take into account the time-dependent phenomena appearing due to the non-stationary electron transport in the active region of a Gunn diode. The fundamental dependencies of the diode current on the carrier diffusion has been also incorporated.

articleTitle: A 45 W class A power amplifier for L-band T/R module
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the paper a high power amplifier with gain of 11 dB and output power of 46.5 dBm for an L-band T/R module is described. Use of a class A amplifier with silicon bipolar transistors reduces nonlinear distortion of the signal.

articleTitle: LF noise and reliability of Gunn diodes
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: On the basis of these investigations it possible to state the following: there is a strong relation between LF noise level and diode technology quality; the relation between LF noise and reliability can be considered mainly as a statistical problem, but for worse technologies the quantity of the test sample may be relatively small; the noise measurement with the aim of reliability estimation is not recommended in the case of commercial semiconductor devices made with the use of high quality technologies, but it is recommended in the case of special and military applications (it is also recommended for new technology preparation); and not only noise level but also noise level changes during initial time of work can be considered as the reliability indicator.

articleTitle: A new ring microstrip diplexer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: An original structure, a method and results of computer-aided synthesis of a new ring microstrip diplexer are considered. These diplexers for matched loads give ideal decoupling between sources and practically pure resistive inputs over the whole frequency band. A scattering matrix for any order filters and results of scattering parameter analysis of ring diplexer when operating into an unmatched load are presented. The frequency characteristics obtained are compared with parameters of a ring hybrid on transmission lines.

articleTitle: Measurement of frequency above 100 GHz with high-Tc Josephson junction array
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: YBaCuO series arrays composed of 23 bicrystal grain boundary Josephson junctions incorporated into 2-arm logarithmic spiral antenna and coupled to a broadband quasi-optic lens system were applied for determination of frequencies above 100 GHz by comparing the DC voltages aroused over the array under MM-wave irradiation, with a solid-state reference cell. Full phase-lock of all junctions under some 0.1 mW incident power at frequency 146 GHz (presence of 23-fold Shapiro step) was obtained for a YSZ-substrate array at temperatures up to 68 K. We verified the precision of the proposed instrument by measuring time frequency drifts for both the 100 GHz Gunn diode oscillator and the 150 GHz backward-wave oscillator.

articleTitle: Complex source point beam scattering and absorption by a lossy circular dielectric cylinder
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this study the problem of the complex source point (CSP) beam scattering and absorption from a lossy circular dielectric cylinder is considered in both E and H polarizations. The algorithm based on recurrent formulas for the numerical calculation of the cylindrical functions with complex arguments has been used. As a result various scattering patterns as well as scattered and absorbed power fractions were calculated for different cylinder parameters.

articleTitle: High resolution radar imaging systems with robust image restoration
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper presents a robust approach to image restoration that combines the properties of classical regularized iterative algorithms and robust features based on the concept of M-estimators. The approach takes into consideration the peculiarities of radar image formation to provide optimal noise removal and image restoration including suppression of ringing, and preservation of edges and fine details.

articleTitle: Global Positioning System using digital beam forming
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Compared with conventional tracking systems the presented tracking system using adaptive beam forming offers the following substantial advantages. The signal to noise ratio is increased. This improves the design margin for future systems. Disturbances of the tracking system by interfering transmitters are suppressed by fading out interrupters selectively. This is based on the following system properties: The additional coarse satellite tracking allows rapid beam forming and tracking of the satellites by the antenna beams. The position and velocity of all transmitters are detected in parallel. Using digital beam forming steering beams are available in very high velocity only limited by the capacity of the processor. Especially for future tracking systems operating in higher frequency bands the application of adaptive beam forming antennas may be necessary in order to obtain the required sensitivity.

articleTitle: Wideband coaxial balun for antenna application
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The modelling and design of a coaxial balun with a balanced-to-unbalanced impedance ratio of 4:1, resulting in a VSWR below 2.0:1 for 4:1 bandwidth, is presented. A modified model is proposed for the coaxial Marchand balun, which takes into account technological discontinuities. The results of simulations are compared with measurement data showing satisfactory agreement between theory and experiment.

articleTitle: The new structures of controllable attenuators
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: New practical circuits for the electrically controllable diode attenuator have been developed. The characteristic feature of the attenuators is a very small phase shift at smooth regulation of the transfer factor. It is shown, that the use of the correction circuits contributes to the essential reduction of the phase shift. For picosecond attenuators the phase stability of 1...5 degrees in working frequency band up to 2 GHz and attenuation range up to 25 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: LF and HF noise of microwave devices
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper the results of an investigation of substrate and surface treatment on LF and HF noise performances of GaAs FETs and Schottky diodes are described. They show that the improvement of LF noise characteristics leads in general to the improvement of HF noise at low current densities, where hot electron noise is negligible.

articleTitle: Review on surveillance sensor tracking
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the paper surveillance sensor tracking is reviewed. It focuses mainly on research done by IRCTR in cooperation with Eurocontrol and NC3A. A survey was made on the groundbased ATC backbone network, tasks for SSR systems using monopulse and advanced algorithms for joint replies, performance evaluation for multi-sensor tracking and on multi sensor tracking in ATC.

articleTitle: Generation of short rise time optical pulses without transient relaxation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A method for generation of optical pulses without transient relaxation and with shortened rise time was suggested and investigated. This method is realised by synchronous irradiation of a pulse modulated laser by another laser at a specified moment.

articleTitle: Scattering of ultrashort electromagnetic pulses by nonlinearly reflecting targets
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The scattering of ultrashort electromagnetic pulses is under investigation numerically by the following models of nonlinear scatterers: nonlinearly loaded vibrator and two-dimensional plate. The calculations carried out give the possibility of determining optimal values of electromagnetic probing pulse duration, to obtain the maximal useful reflected signal at the second harmonic.

articleTitle: Non-symmetrical double-sided slot waveguide and fin-dielectric lines (FDL) as a basis element of three-dimensional integrated circuits of microwave and EHF
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Mathematic models of generalized double-slot waveguide and fin-dielectric line are presented. Some problems of the utilization of these structures for 3D-IC devices are discussed.

articleTitle: Optical testing and annealing of the leukosapphire microwave resonators
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Waveguide-dielectric resonators (WDR) with partial E-and H-plane filling of the waveguide are investigated by optical and microwave means. Some correlation between the microwave and optical properties of high unloaded Q (Q/sub 0//spl ap/2/spl times/10/sup 4/) resonators is found. The optimal regimes of annealing and the resonant frequency temperature drift reduction, are determined. Some examples of the band-pass filter design are presented.

articleTitle: Measurement of complex permittivity and complex permeability of materials
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The time domain measurement of complex permittivity and complex permeability in the 8 to 18 GHz frequency band is considered. Some methods for determination of permittivity and permeability are presented.

articleTitle: Modeling of antennas for mobile communication
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Recent expansion of applications of mobile communication presents new research opportunities and challenges in the design of new antennas and modeling their performance in realistic communication environments. The FDTD method provides an efficient tool for some aspects of design and for modeling of antenna performance in realistic situations. We model the performance of two types of representative antennas, namely: a dual-band strip-sleeve monopole on a laptop computer and a diversity patch antenna on a handset.

articleTitle: Gallium nitride-new material for microwave and optoelectronics
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The first GaAs diodes and field effect transistors (FETs) and the first GaAs/AlGaAs heterojunction FETs (HFETs) and heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs), were followed soon by the devices fabricated utilising the InP based materials, which enabled one to achieve a much higher frequency of operation, speed and much lower noise. Recent achievements in diode and HFET technology utilising GaN based materials proved their potential as power devices, UV photodetectors and in high temperature electronics. In this paper after a brief review of GaN properties as compared with other semiconductors, its technology is briefly described and then the state of the art of GaN based devices is given and its further potential for development shown.

articleTitle: A fast method of calculating noise parameters and its sensitivities [linear multiport circuits]
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new method of calculating signal and noise parameters of linear circuits is based on the nodal circuit approach adapted to facilitate analysis of multiport circuits. Instead of the noise correlation matrix a new efficient matrix description of noise properties, the so called real noise matrix, is used. The new method does not require calculation of the transfer function matrix because the real noise matrix and the admittance matrix are calculated simultaneously. A simulator based on the new method is much faster than a commercial HP MDS simulator.

articleTitle: Radar selected plot processing system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Development of new air sovereignty control system-which is basically the ASOC (Air Sovereignty Operations Center) of Hungary suitable for the present and future is under preparation. This system has extremely high cost of production therefore, not only to prepare it technically, but owing to the fact that existing radar has to be modernized and prepared for connecting to the planned new air sovereignty control system. During preparation time we must pay attention to the following facts: (a) the single reconnaissance sensors have to be integrated into reconnaissance system and in addition the air surveillance has high priority; (b) information of sensors (radar) would have to get through to users within the possible shortest time (within a few seconds); (c) there is great civilian air traffic in peace-time-in case of military threats cooperation between the military and civilian air traffic control has great importance; (d) data of air surveillance has different types of radar we have to use, process in real time and spread information to users according to their requirements. This article is a brief overview of input radar signal processing equipment for the air sovereignty control system having importance especially in field of the radar plot extractors and data processing.

articleTitle: Achievements of European collaboration in CAD within the EDGE project
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper describes the objectives and achievements of a two-year European collaborative project in high-frequency design, which is due to conclude in the first half of 1998. The EDGE project has brought together software developers, users and component manufacturers in a unique partnership which has produced a number of significant technical achievements as well as promoting a more open and flexible concept in creating customised, modular and user-oriented CAD environments.

articleTitle: Complex source radiation in a circular cylindrical radome with grating of lossy strips
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The radiation fields of a line source enclosed by a circular dielectric radome with grating consisting of an array of thin lossy metal strips are analyzed. The variations of the directivity of the source beam with respect to the beam direction are studied. The possibility of damping these variations by an appropriate design of the radome is demonstrated.

articleTitle: CAD for HMICs/MMICs including multilayer structures and MCM technology
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The use of three and more conductor levels in RF, microwave and mm-wave hybrid (HMICs) and monolithic (MMICs) integrated circuits (ICs) and associated recent CAD development work is discussed. Multilayer IC configurations do not only allow compact wiring and interconnection in high speed digital ICs and in Multi-Chip Module (MCM) technology, but also provide new design options for vertically integrated, geometrically compact passive components with hitherto unachieved functionality and electrical performance. Following several years of experience with multilayer design and verification, respective layout-oriented CAD interfaces and algorithms are now reaching a first level of maturity.

articleTitle: A reference source unit for coherent direct synthesizer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The practical realization and measurement results of an L-band reference source are presented. This source unit was designed to be used in frequency synthesizers, especially in a coherent direct synthesizer.

articleTitle: Automatic arbitrary shape optimization based on 3D FD-TD solver and perturbation theory applied for synthesis of resonators
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new efficient method for the automatic design of multimode resonators is presented. Our approach is based on electromagnetic 3-D modelling performed in the optimization loop. The novelty of the method arises from utilization of some information about the electromagnetic field distribution in the decision about the modification of resonator's geometry. The field information is processed using perturbation theory.

articleTitle: Performance of the slotline in the mm-wave range
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper deals with an investigation of the dispersion characteristics of the slotline in the mm-wave range. Attention is paid to the possible excitation of the surface leaky waves on the slotline. Higher order leaky waves were identified on the slotline made on a higher permittivity substrate. Their influence on the line characteristics is evaluated from the view point of practice.

articleTitle: Computer simulation for pulse compression performance analysis
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Pulse compression is a widely used method to maintain the range resolution of radar while increasing the average power per pulse that can be placed on a target. New software was developed which simulates the effects of Doppler shift, additive noise, intrapulse amplitude and phase instability on the compressed radar pulses. In this paper the simulation software tools are described giving some illustrations from the results.

articleTitle: Green's function useful for the analysis of planar structures on multilayered dielectric in cylindrical enclosure
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Green's function for a point charge located inside the multilayered dielectric medium in cylindrical enclosure is derived in a convenient form. The starting inhomogeneous three-dimensional differential equation in cylindrical coordinates is transformed to a one-dimensional equation by applying the variable separation method and orthogonality relations. Final solution is obtained by using the equivalence with a multistep transmission line.

articleTitle: Design of elliptically polarized millimeter wave antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The results of design and investigations of elliptically polarized millimeter wave antenna arrays are shown. A presented leaky-wave antenna array consists of the waveguide structure and a finite diffraction grating. The diffraction grating is excited by an E-type surface wave, which is the eigenwave of the waveguide structure. The diffraction grating consist of rectilinear and parallel nonhomogeneities, which are disposed at an angle of /spl alpha/ in the direction of surface wave propagation. The angle /spl alpha/, widths and distances between nonhomogeneities are chosen by using special optimization algorithms in order to obtain the necessary electrodynamic characteristics.

articleTitle: High power noise sources for L and S band
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: High power noise sources for L and S band with controlled power level were designed. The source output power for L-band is P=12 W and for S-band P=10 W in wide 14% band. The dynamic of power control exceeds 20 dB and flatness is 1 dB. The drop of power outside band is 5 dB/10 MHz for the L-band source and 3 dB/10 MHz for the S-band source.

articleTitle: New mechanism of initiation of negative differential resistance in the structures based on p-n junctions on exposure to microwave radiation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental investigations of the effect of initiation of negative differential resistance on the current-voltage characteristics for diode structures based on p-n-junctions on exposure to high-level power microwave radiation are presented. Under theoretical analysis of the influence of high-level microwave power on the form of I-V characteristics the change of direct current in the diode because of detector effect, the warming up of free charge carriers and nonlinear characteristics of microwave signal reflection from semiconductor structures are considered.

articleTitle: Physics based analytical model for charge storage in an ideal heterostructure barrier varactor
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: An ideal Heterostructure Barrier Varactor (HBV) is defined as a device with no leakage current. Space charge storage in the cladding regions with uniformly doped modulation layers and undoped spacers is analyzed using the Thomas-Fermi equilibrium model and Joyce-Dixon approximation. The resulting Q-V characteristics of the cladding regions are given in closed-form parametric expressions, with the electron concentration as the independent variable. C-V characteristics of the HBV is also given parametrically with charge as the device state variable. The calculated C-V characteristics are in excellent agreement with the measured data.

articleTitle: Computations of 3D electromagnetic field distributions in axially symmetric multilateral dielectric resonators by means of Galerkin-Rayleigh-Ritz method
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Media in the resonators are allowed to have uniaxial dielectric anisotropy. Several field plots are presented for the different resonator structures, including whispering gallery modes in sapphire resonators. Comparitive results are also presented for the structures for which field plots are known.

articleTitle: New designs of the measurement heads for testing Gunn diodes in the 26-40 GHz range
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The aim of this paper was to present two new designs of measurement oscillators for measurements of the generated power and frequency (in the 26-40 GHz range) of Gunn diodes, as well as time dependencies in the case of pulse supply applied to the devices under test. Moreover, measurement heads were built for measurements of Gunn diode chips. The possibility to build generators with nonremovable Gunn diode chips was investigated.

articleTitle: Microstrip disk configuration power divide/combiner modelling using TLM approach
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper a new simple procedure for the analysis of disk configuration microstrip structures is given. The procedure is based on the TLM approach, i.e. on domain segmentation and replacing segments with lumped element circuits. An equivalent circuit representing microstrip structure can be easily solved using any standard electrical CAD program. For three types of subsections (INN, CENT, OUT) appearing in the disk configuration power/divider expression for obtaining equivalent circuits parameters are derived.

articleTitle: Split-duplexer for PCS
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The design and realization of the split-duplexer for the PCS is presented. The split-duplexer has been realized using three comb-line filters. The specific features of the realization involve resonators of various dimensions and filters with additional cross couplings to obtain asymmetric characteristics. A DC-injector has been integrated with the split-duplexer.

articleTitle: Virtual cathode oscillator (vircator) modes
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Vircators as high-power microwave sources have been investigated for twenty years now. Computer simulations are important tools for vircator performance investigations. However, such simulations do not show the mechanisms involved. Two basic mechanisms are usually discussed: Bridges and Birdsall oscillations and Barkhausen-Kurz oscillations. There is also virtual cathode interaction, producing time-of-flight dependent oscillations with restricted frequency. Neglecting this effect may lead to a substantial decrease in energy conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: A generator with frequency synthesis from 2-18 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The principle of operation and measurement results of a generator with direct frequency synthesis is presented. The generator is tuned within the 2-18 GHz frequency range. Its performance includes dense tuning steps, low phase noise level and coherent operation facility with a frequency standard signal.

articleTitle: Application of fast multimodal ABCs in time domain analysis of electromagnetic waves in infinite shielded structures
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper, the application of fast multimodal ABCs for the time domain analysis of the electromagnetic waves in infinite three-dimensional shielded microwave structures is presented. The ABCs are used within a hybrid PEE-FDTD algorithm which combines a classical FDTD method with partial eigenfunction expansion (PEE) scheme. The WG-90 waveguide with a thick asymmetric inductive iris is analysed. The numerical results clearly exhibit the validity and efficiency of the presented algorithm.

articleTitle: Amplified ferrimagnetic echoes in YIG film
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This work is devoted to the nonlinear effects which are connected with parametric interaction of spin waves in ferrites. The number of original results on echo amplification in yttrium iron garnet epitaxial films obtained under uniform magnetic bias field is represented.

articleTitle: Coherent and noncoherent polarimetric radar receivers completely canceling the partially polarized clutter
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Two methods of complete canceling the partially polarized clutter have been described. The first one, called a coherent method, is based on producing a completely polarized receiving vector orthogonal to the instantaneous Jones vector of clutter.
