The other, incoherent method employs three four-vectors perpendicular to the Stokes four-vector of clutter to build the receiving linear combination, closest to the undisturbed signal.

articleTitle: Selected tendencies of modern radars and radar systems development
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper presents modern radars and radar systems problems caused by troubles and dangers connected with actual battlefield conditions. The usefulness of the phased array radar (PAR), low probability of intercept (LPI) radar and the multi-junction radar (MFR) has been described from the point of view of the single radar using. Moreover chosen aspects of the modem radar systems development, including among others over the horizon (OTH) radars and airborne early warning (AEW) radars, has been discussed too.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling of the waveguide antenna array
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new approach in the method of integral equation with separation of the piercing domain is developed. The approach is shown to have a clear geometrical representation: the whole complicated domain of the field determination is subdivided into a number of partial domains and a piercing domain.

articleTitle: Radar signal frequency parameters measurement using compressive receiver
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Frequency parameters are very distinctive features of radar signals. This results both from state of the art in the transmitting techniques and from operational use of radar. The most popular and obvious method to determine signal frequency parameters based on modern technology, is to use a digitizing technique and subsequently the fast Fourier transform algorithm. Such an approach is relatively easy when signal is not limited in time. Faced with this problem, the paper presents the compressive receiver concept with application to measure frequency parameters of a radar signal, which are usually strictly time limited events.

articleTitle: On the skeleton method of pattern synthesis applied to parabolic reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A method of realizing the desired pattern in a plane is demonstrated. The prescribed pattern is replaced by a discrete set of its values, the so called skeleton of the pattern. The problem is reduced to the reconstruction of the skeleton. This is done in an antenna system consisting of a parabolic reflector with a linear array as a primary source.

articleTitle: Wideband analysis of the propagation channel for urban streets at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the propagation channel in the 60 GHz band for a Mobile Broadband System (MBS) typical scenario: an urban street with buildings on both sides. Geometrical optics is used to simulate wave propagation inside the scenario. The wideband characterization of the propagation channel, which is done through the mean delay and the delay spread, is seen to be a function of the propagation scenario conditions. Analytical approximations for these dependencies are presented.

articleTitle: Plasma objects diagnostic using transitional radiation of the electron bunches
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The diagnostics of the density profile and other parameters of inhomogeneous plasma devices using the transitional radiation of modulated electron beams or charged bunches moving through these devices is proposed in theory.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional modelling of the thermal properties of Gunn diodes
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper describes two-dimensional modelling of the X-band Gunn diode using a differential numerical method. By comparing the results with the measurements, the conclusions on diode quality can be stated.

articleTitle: A new type of high power passive limiter
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new type of passive limiter structure is presented in the paper. The frequency response of the limiter for low power signals are pass-band type with high attenuation outside the described frequency range. For high power signals, when the limiting process occurs, the attenuation remains more than 30 dB over wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Performances of optical PD-FSK systems corrupted by interchannel interference and intersymbol interference
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper, performances of a phase diversity FSK system in the presence of thermal noise, laser phase noise, interchannel interference and intersymbol interference are calculated. It is shown that interchannel interference and intersymbol interference lead to significant performance degradation for coherent systems. Obtained results are shown graphically.

articleTitle: Modeling of the influence of the contact's interface on series resistance of high-electron mobility transistor and calculating of microwave performance using HELENA's software
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In order to predict microwave performance of a High-Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT), the simulator HELENA may be used. This software allows us to calculate the microwave parameters depending on the series resistance of the transistor. To exactly determine the series resistance a way to calculate the value of contact resistance is required. A new approach to evaluate the ohmic contact resistance of the HEMT (based on the AlGaAs-GaAs heterostructure) including the non-uniform interface is presented for the first time. A model is presented where the value of the contact resistance depends on the density of metallic "spikes" at the interface. Regarding the physical parameters of the heterostructure and topology of the designed transistor, we calculated the series resistance in the range between 0.2 to 1.2 /spl Omega/mm (in dependence on the processing of the contact). The microwave parameters of the transistor (designed in our laboratory) was calculated using the software HELENA. Results of the simulation confirm the essential influence of contact resistance on the microwave performance.

articleTitle: Injection problem in powerful quasi-optical modulator
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Theoretical investigation of injection problem in powerful quasi-optical modulators is presented. It is shown that the possibility of increasing current and the level of controlling power is thanks to the optimal regime of injection for surface integrated p-i-n structure with "deep" junctions. The increase of the diffusion coefficient due to existing electromagnetic wave and the criterion of high-power wave are obtained.

articleTitle: Comparison of designing methods concerning E-plane rectangular waveguide step transformers
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The results of computations and simulations of E-plane waveguide step transformers, as well as their comparison with experimental data, are presented in this paper. Several conclusions are formulated based on the theoretical and practical responses presented here.

articleTitle: Interdigital transducers for piezoelectric interfacial waves
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Piezoelectric interfacial waves (PIWs) propagate along conducting planes embedded in piezoelectric crystals: shortening of the electric field by the plane reduces the elastic wave velocity and provides the waveguiding mechanism. Propagating inside the body, PIWs are well protected from environmental interference and thus, PIWs are interesting for applications in highly stable devices, filters and piezoelectric resonators. In this paper, the problem of generation and detection of PIWs by interdigital transducers (IDTs) is considered, the IDTs widely used in SAW technology. The theory is developed accounting for bulk waves that are generated and transmitted between two uniform IDTs.

articleTitle: Measurement methods of a directly modulated DFB laser chirp
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Direct measurements of DFB laser chirp, by means of an optical spectrum analyzer, are presented. A numerical simulation of the measurement setup is performed. A good agreement is achieved between the simulated and measured data.

articleTitle: Application of microwave non-destructive research-measurement method in evaluation of adhesion properties of paint coatings
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Both theoretical and experimental work on the microwave electromagnetic non-destructive testing of adhesion are presented. It is shown that definite testing is possible with multi-frequency sounding and solution of the inverse problem.

articleTitle: High-efficiency power amplifier CAD
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A CAD tool for the semi-automatic synthesis of high-efficiency microwave power amplifiers is presented. The basic theory and the implementation of the algorithm, based on the simultaneous and consistent solution of circuit equations together with design goals, are illustrated. The tool allows the designer to obtain a pre-optimised power stage in terms of input and output optimum loads at fundamental and harmonic frequencies.

articleTitle: Broadband low noise optical receiver utilizing distributed amplification
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new approach for the design and construction of low noise broadband optical receivers is presented utilizing distributed amplification based on hybrid integrated technology. Using extremely low noise PHEMTs as well as appropriate matching between the photodiode and the distributed amplifier result in a fairly low input equivalent noise current (10 pA//spl radic/(Hz)). Due to the high capacitance bypass capacitors, the lower edge of the transmission band is decreased which is important for many applications.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of connectors for coplanar waveguide circuits
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Two types of coaxial connectors for feeding of hybrid integrated coplanar waveguide circuits have been designed. The contact with ground planes is provided by push-fit mounted contact tabs. These connectors may be fully characterized using recently developed resonance measurement based method. Two examples of characterization results have been given for connectors intended for use through the X and K band, respectively.

articleTitle: Electrostatic analysis of a coupler with a multiwire microwave line
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Numerical electrostatic analysis of a coupler with a multiwire microwave line is presented. The coupler was patented by the Telecommunications Research Institute in 1992. The results of numerical analysis confirm the results of practical realisation obtained experimentally. An electrostatic analysis method of a complex transmission structures with multiwire microwave lines is also described.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of the conductivity time-dependence in a half space by scattering fields
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The inverse problem for a half-space with time-varying conductivity is solved analytically. The incident field here has an arbitrary form so the results could be used for signals as well as for waves. The conductivity time-dependence is determined in two variants: (1) by the incident field and the field inside the transient region and (2) by incident field and the external field.

articleTitle: The microscopic Monte Carlo technique of the millimetre-wave unipolar devices simulation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new efficient method of the electron's wave vector calculation after its ionised impurity scattering is discussed in this paper. The accent has been put on the fact that the electron scattering on ionised impurities plays an important role in hot carrier diffusion noise of the millimetre-wave devices based on the highly doped gallium arsenide. The characteristics of the GaAs millimetre-wave FETs with a quarter-micrometer gate were analysed.

articleTitle: Injection-locked oscillator arrays based on CPW-fed antennas
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Oscillating microstrip antennas fed by coplanar waveguide and using GaAs MESFETs have been designed and characterised at /spl sim/4 GHz. The association of these active antennas has permitted us to obtain steerable arrays by tuning the DC bias voltages of the oscillators. The use of a PIN diode switch is presented as a mean to extend the phase control of the radiated signal to 360/spl deg/ and to obtain wide beam scanning.

articleTitle: C-band coherent direct synthesizer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The principle of operation of a direct coherent synthesizer is described. Practical realisation and measurement results of the C-band synthesizer are presented. Good parameters such as small frequency steps, fast switching time and low phase noise level are obtained.

articleTitle: The development of the GaAs MMICs for radiocommunication and radar applications at the Warsaw University of Technology
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper presents an overview of several GaAs microwave monolithic integrated circuits designed at the Institute of Electronics Fundamentals intended for applications in various radiocommunication and radar systems and also used in education in MMIC design. Circuits covering frequencies 1 GHz to 23 GHz and their main features are shown.

articleTitle: The formation of polarized radiation by layered-inhomogeneous media
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The radiometric systems of remote sensing carry out researches of Earth cover on the basis of the surface microwave radiation analyses. For increase of efficiency and reliability of this analysis it is necessary to know and to understand process of formation of radiothermal microwave radiation in media. The general principles of formation of microwave radiation of media are well known; in view of the large variety of various surfaces many questions of the thermal radioemission theory have not been investigated, especially for surfaces having a complex structure. The interest in this direction is caused by layered-inhomogenous media. In this work we take advantage of a method of analysis, based on determination of thermal losses of auxiliary flat electromagnetic waves, radiating on a surface in a direction opposite to that for which radiating properties of a media are determined. Using the theorem of reciprocity the polarising properties of thermal radioemission are determined by laws of polarized absorption of this wave.

articleTitle: Improved analysis of dispersion characteristics of a high permittivity rectangular dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: New and simple analytical methods for propagation constants of a high permittivity rectangular dielectric waveguide are presented. At first, we determine an infinite number of candidates for eigenvalue pair (k/sub x/,k/sub y/) by eigenvalue equation derived from main electromagnetic fields of the mode. Next, we select a correct eigenvalue pair by minimizing a discontinuity of secondary components on the boundaries. Our numerical results show a good agreement with that of previous numerical methods even for high permittivity.

articleTitle: Measurement of level ratio and phase response uncertainty of dispersed/compressed pulse radar transmitting chains using microwave receiver
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The microwave receiver OPM-121 providing automated measurement of relative side-to-main-lobe amplitude ratio of dispersed/compressed pulse radar transmitting chains operating in the L-band is presented. It also enables evaluation of phase response uncertainty using an AM pulse sequence. The instrument performance includes statistical phase and amplitude data processing. The OPM-121 may prove useful as a tool for diagnosis and fault finding in radar transmitters.

articleTitle: Waveguide-resonance method of dielectrometry
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Problem of rectangular waveguide H10 wave resonance diffraction on the dielectric specimen of the parallelepiped shape is solved. The dielectric specimen fills the waveguide completely along its narrow walls. A mathematical model is constructed for the waveguide measurement of the specimen complex permittivity.

articleTitle: Propagation in ferrite microstrip structures magnetised longitudinally
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Spectral domain analysis of single and coupled microstrip line with longitudinally magnetised ferrite substrate is presented. The dispersion characteristics of the fundamental modes are investigated. The effect of the cut-off frequency is explained on the case of coupled mode approach.

articleTitle: Low-field electron transport mechanism in GaAs Gunn diodes and GaAs/GaAs/sub ins/ layers (MBE)
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: We present the basis of resistance calculations of Gunn diodes in a magnetic field and its dependence on field direction angle to the diode plane. Also the influence on the experimental results of diode electrode shape is considered. The current transport between electrodes and diode subsurface layers is shown to be tunnelling. For comparison the transport properties of thin GaAs/GaAs/sub ins/ layers are presented. The transport in the thin Gunn diodes layers is significantly better. We consider that the cause of such behaviour is the lower compensation ratio in the VPE layers of Gunn diodes material in contrast to MBE epitaxial layers.

articleTitle: The artificial intelligence tools utilization in radar signal processing
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper presents the problem of flying objects recognition with the utilization of artificial intelligence tools. There are two basic tools-neural network and expert system. The neural network used for the object features values extraction has been presented. The extraction method of the radar signal from radar to the neural network has been presented also. Moreover, this paper describes these tools. They are very useful for flying object recognition particularly when they collaborate.

articleTitle: Geometric phase for the far zone field of a cylindrical dielectric resonator aperture antenna
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new aspect of the far zone field of aperture antenna-a decomposition of the total phase of the field into a dynamical and a geometrical part-is presented in this report. Characteristic features of geometric phase are given for the case of a cylindrical dielectric resonator aperture antenna.

articleTitle: Submillimeter wave hot electron bolometer mixers
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper, an overview is given of hot-electron superconducting mixers for submillimeter wave applications. The two competing types of mixers, the phonon cooled and the diffusion cooled, are described. The mixer conversion properties can be calculated if the I-V characteristic of the unpumped device is known. The influence of image frequency power dissipation is analyzed. Finally, state of the art results are presented.

articleTitle: A set-up for measurement of high-power coupler directivity
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A set-up to measure coupler directivity with high levels of microwave power is proposed. Measuring procedures as well as error analysis are presented. Using a fixed attenuator differently placed in the circuit a measured directivity range is extended although typical microwave detectors are used in the set-up configuration. An influence of high power level on coupler directivity value can be detected applying the presented set-up.

articleTitle: Calibration procedure and experimental results of a dual six-port network analyzer with phase-sensitive homodyne detectors
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper presents some aspects of the new concept of the homodyne dual six-port network analyzer. The paper reminds us of the general idea of this type of network analyzer. It contains the principle of the standard calibration procedure. Both the results of experiments and comparison of accuracy between a typical network analyzer and the discussed measurement system are also presented.

articleTitle: A new computer program for microwave Schottky diode structures analysis and design
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the paper a new computer program for the silicon Schottky diode structures analysis has been presented. It constitutes a user friendly tool for computer-aided design of the diode structures for a given frequency band. The program makes it possible to compute the most important DC characteristics of the diode, taking into account nonideality of the metal-semiconductor junction, existence of the thin insulating film in the M-S interface and the influence of the geometrical configuration of electrodes on the series resistance of the diode.

articleTitle: Integrated set of instruments for transmission's performance measurements in radar systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper, the authors present a method of radar signal generation with an integrated set of instruments. These signals can have various forms and properties and can be used to test any device or block of devices in radar systems. The results of testing a quadrature phase detector as an example of a device under test are presented additionally.

articleTitle: Medical diagnostic ultrasound: radar roots and recent developments
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Radar, sonar and medical ultrasonics exploit imaging techniques for detection of the position and backscattering/reflection strength of the target and its velocity. Velocity sensing techniques can be as simple as CW Doppler up to the multi-channel MTI. Imaging and Doppler ultrasonics creatively employing recent radar and sonar technologies are rapidly growing with numerous new exciting developments. High density, multi-elements linear array, phase array and annular array transducers benefit from the synthetic aperture and open a new era of a real time scanning of the biological structures with unprecedented quality. Color coding, tissue Doppler, contrast agents echo enhancement and other new, exciting developments are discussed.

articleTitle: Gunn diodes for 26-40 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The technology of GaAs MBE layers for K-band Gunn diodes is described in the paper along with the method of diode structure preparation. Chips were assembled directly in a microwave generator. The design of measurement circuit and microwave generator, as well as results of experiments are presented.

articleTitle: Modeling of performance of wireless communication antennas in the vicinity of the user
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Many wireless communication devices are used with their antennas in close proximity of the human head. This results in changes in the antenna characteristics that affect the communications performance and in the deposition of microwave energy in the user's head that for some devices may be in excess of the values allowed by health protection standards. These effects are evaluated using the FDTD method for two new types of antennas and the results are compared to those for a generic monopole handset.

articleTitle: High-directivity multilayer coupler
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new edge coupled microstrip coupler with high level of directivity is proposed. A multilayer structure to equalise phase velocities of even and odd modes is used. The frequency characteristics achieved show good agreement of simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: High temperature superconducting films and HTS devices for wireless communication systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: HTS films exhibit very low losses, and HTS microstrip filters ensure a low noise figure and sharp skirts when employed in cellular base station receivers. This paper reviews the current state of the art in the field of microwave applications of superconducting thin films and of problems related to nonlinear power effects in HTS materials.

articleTitle: Power microwave amplifiers based on aluminium oxide substrates
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In this paper we will describe the application of new technology for creation of the power amplifiers. Using high heat conduction aluminium base substrate is very important for power circuits. Output power of the microwave amplifier is 1 W at f=1.7...2.0 GHz. Gain is 40 dB at compression of pre-amplification 1 dB.

articleTitle: Improved excitation model for FDTD analysis of mobile phone antennas
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The practical FDTD analysis of personal communications devices requires simplified models of antenna excitation. The paper reviews the existing models and proposes a new improved one based on a thin feeding TEM line with a square cross-section and modal template termination. The new model ensures excellent accuracy of return loss extraction even at coarse discretization, and competitive speed in calculating antenna efficiency.

articleTitle: Nondestructive microwave measurements of dielectric materials
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Nondestructive microwave dielectric measurements based on open-ended rectangular waveguide and coaxial line sensors are considered. The errors in the dielectric constant measurements due to the uncertainties of the measuring instruments are calculated and compared for the two types of sensors. A comparison based on advantages and disadvantages for both sensors is also presented.

articleTitle: The fast-tuned low phase noise source for C band
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper presents the design of the fast-tuned low phase noise signal source for C band with many applications in the radar device domain. The operation of this electronic system is described The results of measurements done for the constructed heterodyne are also included.

articleTitle: RF- and noise characterisation of MOSFETs for mobile communications applications
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: We present noise characterisations of silicon MOSFETs in terms of the four noise parameters from 150 MHz to 20 GHz. A special tuner system was designed and built to measure below 1 GHz. Additionally we present S-parameter measurements and show the good correspondence which can be achieved between measured and simulated S-parameters based on the extracted small signal elements.

articleTitle: Calibration of the PTP vector network analyzer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A calibration procedure for perturbation two-port vector network analyzer (PTP VNA) is presented. PTP VNA consists of a variable perturbation two-port (PTP) placed between a device under test (DUT) and a scalar network analyzer (SNA). A vector reflection coefficient of the DUT is determined on the basis of amplitude only measurements. A full correction of SNA systematic errors is possible. In principle it may be used up to millimetre and submillimetre frequency bands.

articleTitle: Linear antenna array on a multilayer dielectric
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This work presents the concept of a linear antenna array mounted on a multilayer dielectric substrate. The results of measurements are compared with theoretical calculations. The analysis was made with the use of the moment method and Green function for the multilayer array.

articleTitle: Transmission line method for liquid or loose material diagnosis
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A method for complex permittivity and permeability determination of liquid and loose materials is presented. A general case of the reflection and transmission method is considered and proper equations are derived. A particular case based on the reflection coefficient measurements of two samples of different lengths is studied in detail. Some uncertainty problems are discussed.

articleTitle: Dividing unit as K-invertor in some types of diplexers
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A new procedure for compact diplexer design is proposed. It consists of the integration of a dividing unit and the first K-invertors of channel filters and is based on an exact calculation of S-matrices of the combined waveguide units. As a result essential reduction of diplexer length without a degradation of frequency response has been obtained.

articleTitle: PIW/SAW multistrip coupler working at Bragg conditions
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A multistrip coupler (MSC) is one of the most important device in SAW technology. It couples two acoustic channels in SAW filters and resonators. The analysis presented here concerns primarily the later application generalized to piezoelectric interfacial waves (PIWs). In Bragg conditions, the reflection of PIWs or SAWs from MSC strips is the reason for severe distortion of its frequency characteristic and cannot be neglected in the analysis. A rigorous theory of MSC is developed accounting for both electric, and mechanical interactions of MSC strips with the SAW that results in Bragg reflection from the strips. Bulk waves are neglected.

articleTitle: Error probability of PSK satellite communication system in the presence of noise and noisy carrier reference signal
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A PSK satellite communication system consisting of earth transmitter station, uplink, satellite station, downlink and earth receiver station is considered in this paper. The synchronization reference signal is extracted by the first-order nonlinear PLL and, by assumption, this extraction is not ideal. The uplink noise influence is considered through the frequency offset of signal remitted by the satellite station (the narrowband process phase derivative fluctuations), while the downlink noise is taken into consideration through the error probability expression. The steady-state p.d.f. of phase error p(/spl phi/) for the observed system is determined as well as the total error probability P/sub c/.

articleTitle: Four wave acousto-electromagnetic interactions in crystals with a nonlinear electrostriction
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The four wave parametric interactions of microwave acoustic waves with powerful electromagnetic radiation in the strong nonlinear regime is investigated. The interaction is due to account of the fourth order terms in the expansion of the free energy of the anisotropic crystal. It is shown, that the instability and the parametrical increasing of the waves' amplitudes in a system takes place. This leads to shaping of the spatially inhomogeneous structures. The velocity of propagation of those structures is smaller than the sound velocity in such a crystal.

articleTitle: Performances degradation of digital fiber optic systems due to modal noise
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In long distance fiber optic communication systems, the influence of modal noise on the system performances is very important. Modal noise mostly arises in the splice of two fibers or due to an imperfect connectors. The circuit noise is also incorporated in the analysis and hence the bit error rate versus input optical power is derived. The bit error rate degradation due to modal noise is presented.

articleTitle: Linear slot array feeded by corrugated waveguide
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: This paper describes the realisation and measurements of a slot array where slots are fed by a highly dispersive corrugated waveguide. The influence of various technological restrictions on the waveguide properties is presented.

articleTitle: Development of novel semiconductor devices
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The physical background of novel small-scale fast semiconductor devices has been presented. The performance constrains of hot electron and quantum devices have been discussed. The prospects of development and application of these devices has been indicated. Experimental structures studied at the Institute of Electronic Materials Technology and technologies needed for their realisation have also been presented.

articleTitle: Recent advances in metrology for the electromagnetic characterization of materials at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: An overview is presented of recent advances realized in the methods of measuring the complex permittivity, (/spl epsiv//sup */=/spl epsiv/'-j/spl epsiv/"), complex permeability (/spl mu/*=/spl mu/'-j/spl mu/") and RF surface impedance of electronic materials. We discuss a variety of different measurement techniques, including their relevant advantages and disadvantages. Nondestructive methods, that are important in material production quality control, are emphasized. Accurate measurements of low-loss materials (/spl epsiv/", /spl mu/"<0.01) require high-Q resonator techniques. Many examples of these are presented, including the TE/sub 01p/ mode cylindrical cavity, the split post dielectric resonator for characterizing flat sheets, the dielectric rod resonator for measuring the RF surface resistance of superconductors, and the whispering gallery mode technique which provides the highest known sensitivity for dielectric loss measurements. Measurements of medium-to high-loss materials (/spl epsiv/", /spl mu/">0.1) are best performed using broadband free-space methods as well as transmission line techniques, such as waveguide, coaxial air line or the open-ended coax probe.

articleTitle: Photonic technology for microwave engineering
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper presents a review of photonic devices and technology applications in microwave systems. Four fundamental applications are discussed: transmission of microwave signals by optical links, use of photonic devices for generation and controlling of microwave signals, principles of operation of phase-arrayed antennas with photonic transmission, and finally, microwave measurements methods with photonic techniques.

articleTitle: Microwave permittivity determination in agricultural products
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Applications of microwave measurement techniques for determining the permittivity of agricultural products (seeds, plants, grains, fruits, meat, etc.) are reviewed. After explaining the principles of measurements, some numerical values are given and future prospects are discussed.

articleTitle: Antennas and human in personal communications: applications of modern EM computational techniques
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The evolution of wireless personal communications has necessitated the comprehensive understanding of electromagnetic (EM) interactions between handset antennas and a nearby human body. These human-antenna interaction affects the electromagnetic performance of the antenna by changing antenna input impedance, by modifying the antenna radiation patterns and by absorbing antenna delivered power. Recently, the advanced numerical techniques-e.g. the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) and the Eigenfunction Expansion Method (EEM)-have allowed the detailed study of the antenna properties In the vicinity of human tissues with various antenna configurations. Currently, several research groups around the world have undertaken the assessment of technical requirements for the compliance testing of the handset antennas. Accurate investigation of these EM interactions will lead to new antenna designs which are less susceptible to the human biological tissue. In this paper, we discuss the computed EM interaction results from the FDTD method with an anatomical human tissue model. In addition, useful engineering data for the antenna design are provided based on the EEM computation.

articleTitle: Microwave emitter position location: present and future
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Position location (determination) of enemy microwave emitters (radars and jammers) is one of the most important tasks of electronic warfare (EW) systems, particularly for electronic intelligence (ELINT) and electronic support measures (ESM) systems. Correctly performed location of those emitters yields data allowing one to deduce an allocation of enemy radar-controlled weapon systems, to detect associated threats and makes possible the elimination of the emitters from a battlefield by jamming or missiles (weapon delivery). Effectiveness of emitter location is a significant condition of successful military action. Since the contemporary battlefield is more and more saturated by electronic systems, thus the significance of location systems using sophisticated emitter location techniques and algorithms (ELT&A) will be permanently increasing. This paper provides a comprehensive review, presenting current state of knowledge concerning ELT&A including the most important technological and theoretical aspects of emitter location.

articleTitle: Advances in polarimetric SAR interferometry and its application to geo/eco-environmental stress change monitoring
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Radar polarimetry has established itself in high resolution POL-SAR imaging, image target characterization and selective image feature extraction. With the addition of single platform dual antenna interferometers, digital elevation mapping (DEM) was made possible (which can be recovered in most cases equally well from standard fully polarimetric POL-SAR image data utilizing the Schuler purely polarimetric DEM algorithms not requiring an interferometer). In order to be able to fully describe direction-sensitive environmental stress changes, it is necessary to rapidly advance repeat-pass (RP) fully polarimetric (POL: scattering matrix) differential (D) interferometric (In) SAR imaging systems (RP-POL-D-InSAR) which have emerged with the SIR-C/X-SAR Missions 1 and 2. In pursuing this goal, Cloude and Pottier (1997) introduced the polarimetric entropy/anisotropy method and Cloude and Papathanassiou (1997) introduced the polarimetric-interferometric phase coherence optimization (PIPCO) procedure. This PIPCO procedure is verified in this paper by utilizing an ideally matching repeat-pass pair of the SIR-C/X-SAR Mission 2, Tien-Shan tracks within the Russian Academy of Sciences, Siberian Division, Buriat Natural Science Center (RAS-SD-BNSC) SE Baikal Lake, Selenga Delta (Kabansk-Kudara-Oymur: 52.16/spl deg/ N, 106.67/spl deg/ E) Geo-environmental Sanctuary, the "Kudara Polygon" for which various institutes of RAS-SD-BNSC have collected extensive geographic (geo-ecological and geo- tectonic) environmental information and vegetative groundtruth data over several decades.

articleTitle: Si and SiGe millimeterwave integrated circuits for sensor and communications applications
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Silicon based monolithic integrated millimeter-wave circuits have been suggested in 1981 by the RCA group of A. Rosen et al. Since 1986 in the field of silicon monolithic millimeter-wave integrated circuits (SIMMWICs) there are increasing research activities at the former AEG-Telefunken Research Institute which has merged now into the Daimler-Benz Research Center and at the Technische Universitat Munchen. Up to now SIMMWICs for frequencies up to above 100 GHz have already been fabricated, and the suitability of silicon as the substrate material for monolithic integrated millimeter-wave circuits has been successfully demonstrated. The SiGe heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) is a promising candidate for silicon based monolithic integrated millimeter-wave circuits. The IMPATT diode provides high oscillator output power combined with high efficiency. Monolithic integration of solid-state devices provides the possibility of low-cost production, improved reliability, small size and light weight, and easy assembly. The linear passive parts of SIMMWICs may be realized in planar circuit technology. In the frequency region above 60 GHz SIMMWICs of only a few millimeters size may also include planar antenna structures. The integration of the antenna structures allows the direct coupling of SIMMWICs to the radiation field. Monolithic integrated millimeter-wave circuits based on silicon and SiGe will give new options for millimeter-wave sensor and communication applications.

articleTitle: Simultaneous noise and vector network analysis using radiometer systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Advances of an original noise measurement approach to simultaneous noise and small-signal characterization of networks are presented. This approach features the use of natural noise for exciting the device under test (DUT) and a radiometer for measuring the response from which the DUT's scattering and noise parameters are then extracted. Different radiometer systems for measurements of one- and two-port devices are considered. They, like a conventional vector network analyzer, need to be calibrated before the measurement. The simplest arrangement, called the multistate radiometer, is a single-channel instrument that measures both the reflection coefficient and the noise temperature of one-port DUTs. Using a pull-source technique, it can be utilized also for a complete characterization of two-port DUTs. Other systems, based on multi-channel radiometers, can perform the same measurements in a more natural way, i.e. by gauging appropriate noise waves at the DUT ports. However, this calls for a more complex instrument design and mathematical model than for the multistate radiometer. The paper presents experimental data showing real capabilities of the multistate radiometer as well as analyses and simulations of the measurement uncertainties achievable with several different multi-channel radiometer systems.

articleTitle: Millimeter and submillimeter wave mixers based on superconducting weak links
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: Principles of operation of superconducting mixers based on: Superconductor-Insulator-Superconductor (SIS) tunnel junctions, Josephson junctions in high temperature superconductors and on superconducting hot-electron-microbolometers are presented. Most recent results on all types of superconducting mixers, with special attention paid to noise properties is reviewed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic compatibility of electronic equipment-review of testing methods
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper presents a direct and an indirect method by which the electromagnetic compatibility of electronic equipment can be tested. Most of the tests were run at the EMC Laboratory Institute of Telecommunication and acoustics, Wroclaw University of Technology.

articleTitle: Developments in radar waveform design
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The design of radar waveforms has made significant advances over the past two decades. This has been prompted both by increasingly stringent radar performance requirements and the development of high-speed digital processing hardware. The purpose of this paper is to review two specific examples of modern waveform design, and to attempt to make some predictions for the future.

articleTitle: Coping with numerical complexity in computational electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: The paper presents a selection of techniques that are currently being investigated at the Technical University of Gdansk and can be used to accelerate the computation of high and low frequency electromagnetic fields. The techniques discussed represent three different strategies leading to the reduction of solution times in frequency and time domain simulations. The first strategy uses new numerical techniques which offer near optimal numerical cost of solving large sparse linear systems of equations resulting from the discretization of partial differential equations. The second strategy involves taking advantage of the recent developments in computer hardware namely the SMP and scalable parallel architectures. Finally, the third one aims at finding a better field representation or problem parameterization and results in algorithms which are particularly useful in problems requiring repetitive calculations that are often encountered in computational electromagnetics.

articleTitle: An MMIC family for particle detector readout electronics
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: A family of GaAs monolithic front-end amplifiers, to be used in a large number of applications in present and future radiation detection experimental apparatus, is described in this paper. Design, realization and measurements are presented for MMICs especially designed for front-ends for RPC and GaAs cosmic ray detectors, among which a logarithmic amplifier, fiber optic and cable front-ends for data transmissions up to 2.5 Gbit/s, including ultra-fast pulse amplifiers up to 5 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Radio astronomy in Ukraine
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Microwaves and Radar. MIKON-98. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.98EX195)
abstract: In the Ukraine there are some very advanced radio astronomical techniques for every frequency range. A great amount of data has been obtained with the world biggest instruments in the decametric range-radio telescope UTR-2 and VLBI system URAN. Active work is being carried out on the antenna RT-70 for centimetric and decimetric ranges and on the antenna RT-22 for the millimetric range. Existing scientific experience and technical potential with close international collaboration provide great opportunities for further development of all frequencies of radio astronomy in the Ukraine.
